title: How to connect multiple Notion workspaces to Claude or ChatGPT
summary: Connect multiple Notion workspaces to Claude or ChatGPT with Nango. Find meeting notes in one workspace and create a summary in another.
body_markdown:
The official Notion connector for Claude or ChatGPT[supports only one Notion workspace at a time](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-ai-mcp/issues/178) . So it’s not very useful for people who work with multiple Notion workspaces.


In this tutorial, we’ll show you how to connect multiple Notion workspaces to Claude, ChatGPT, or any agent that supports MCPs. Setup is free and should take about five minutes.


To make both workspaces available in one chat, we’ll use[Nango](https://nango.dev/) and its Management MCP. The[free plan allows up to 10 connections](https://nango.dev/pricing) (accommodates multiple Notion workspaces and other apps you connect).


## Why use Nango instead of the official Notion connector?


The official Notion connector works well for one workspace you own. Nango makes more sense when your work spans several workspaces, other people’s workspaces, and apps other than just Notion.


Official Notion connector Nango


Multiple Notion workspaces in one chat No, one workspace at a time Yes


Someone else authorizes their workspace (for example, a client) No, you sign in yourself Yes, with a share link. They don't need a Nango account


Limit access to specific pages No, it uses your full Notion permissions Yes, you pick the pages during setup


Query large databases on Free and Plus plans Partial, full querying needs Business or Enterprise with Notion AI Yes


Notion plus Slack, Gmail, Linear, and other apps in one connection No Yes, with a single Nango connector install in Claude/ChatGPT


Nango also supports[Notion’s official MCP server](https://nango.dev/api-integrations/notion-mcp) as a passthrough so your agent can use those tools alongside Nango’s prebuilt tools for Notion.


## Step 1: Add Notion in Nango


Sign in to[Nango](https://app.nango.dev/) or[create a free account](https://app.nango.dev/signup) . In **Catalog** , search for Notion. Select the regular **Notion** entry with the **Instant setup** label, rather than Notion (MCP).


On Notion’s details page, click **Add integration** and keep Nango’s managed OAuth app.


**Quick info:** The managed app lets you connect your workspaces without creating a public integration in Notion’s developer portal.


Once Notion is set up, **Add test connection** appears on its page. Use it to connect the workspace that holds your meeting notes.


## Step 2: Connect more Notion workspaces


1. Click **Add test connection** , select **Notion** , and click **Connect** . In the **Link Notion Account** dialog, click **Connect** again.


1. Sign in to Notion and choose the workspace that holds your meeting notes. With that workspace selected, click **Select pages** .


1. The page picker lists pages you have full access to. Select the meeting notes and click **Allow access** . Your agent can see only the pages you share here and their accessible subpages.


1. After authorization, return to Nango and open **Connections** . You’ll see one Notion entry for the workspace you just connected.
2. To connect the workspace where the summary will go, click **Add test connection** again, select **Notion** , and repeat the flow. Choose your second workspace, Client Demo in our example, then select its **Launch Tracker** page and click **Allow access** .


If the second workspace belongs to a client and you aren’t a member, use **Share connect link** instead. Send it to a member who can authorize Nango; guests cannot add new connections. The recipient doesn’t need a Nango account, and the link expires after 30 minutes. If Enterprise settings block installation, ask the workspace owner to approve or connect Nango.


Once both workspaces are authorized, return to **Connections** and look for two Notion entries. Both rows can show your Nango email in the Customer column, so you’ll confirm their workspace names from your chat in Step 4. To add more workspaces, repeat the same connection flow.


**Adding pages later:** The person who authorized the connection can open another page they have full access to, then choose **••• → More → Connections → Add connections → Nango** .


## Step 3: Enable Nango in Claude or ChatGPT


With both workspaces connected to Nango, choose the assistant you want to use below.


### Claude


1. Open **Plugins** in the sidebar and search for Nango, or open the[Nango connector listing](https://claude.ai/directory/3822f3b8-11cd-4f4c-bbe7-2a9ec6be28b9) .
2. Select **Connect to Claude** . Sign in to the Nango account containing your Notion connections and approve access.


1. Check that Nango shows **Connected** , then start a new chat.


In the new chat’s message box, open **+ → Plugins** , search for Nango, and make sure its toggle is on.


On Claude Team or Enterprise, an organization owner may need to enable Nango first.


### ChatGPT


In ChatGPT on the web, go to **Plugins → Add → Add custom MCP server** .


In the setup form, name the app **Nango** , enter` https://mcp.nango.dev/mcp` as the server URL, and choose **OAuth** . If asked for a client registration method, select **CIMD** . Review the setup warning and check **I understand and want to continue** , then select **Create as a plugin** and install it.


Select **Continue to Nango** to sign in to the account containing your Notion connections, then approve access. Once connected, start a new chat, type **@** , and select Nango. Custom plugins and write actions depend on your plan and workspace permissions.


To use these workspaces in Codex, Cursor, or Claude Code, follow[Nango’s coding-agent setup instructions](https://nango.dev/docs/getting-started/coding-agent-setup) . Connect your agent to the same Nango account with the required access, and your existing Notion connections carry over.


## Step 4: Start querying connected Notion workspaces with Claude/ChatGPT


With Nango enabled, first check that your assistant can see both workspaces. In your new chat, ask:


> List all Notion workspaces connected via Nango.


**Quick info:** Your agent uses Nango’s prebuilt Notion tools to search and read pages, create and update pages, work with comments, and query databases, subject to the permissions you granted.


### Turn meeting notes into a client summary


In our example, the meeting notes are in Emmanuel Oyibo, with “Q4 launch” and the meeting dates in their title. The destination page, Launch Tracker, is in Client Demo. Ask your agent to turn those notes into a summary under the tracker:


> Find last week’s meeting notes about the Q4 launch in my Emmanuel Oyibo workspace and add a summary page under Launch Tracker in my Client Demo workspace.


Review any request to create the page. Once your agent confirms that the summary is ready, open the Notion link in its response.


In Notion, check that the summary appears beneath Launch Tracker in Client Demo and includes the decisions and action items from your notes. Your own Notion account needs access to open the page.


## Connecting more apps to your agent with Nango


You can extend this workflow to the other apps you use alongside Notion, such as Google Drive, Slack, Linear, Gmail, Jira, or Confluence. Nango supports authentication for[1,400+ APIs and MCPs](https://nango.dev/api-integrations) , and new connections become available through the Nango MCP you’ve already installed, with the access you’ve granted.
